outcome: One consistent access policy follows every user, whether they are at a depot, working from home or on the road.
overview: A logistics operator’s users are rarely where the security controls are — drivers on handhelds, depot staff on links nobody would call enterprise, planners at home — and backhauling all of that to a data centre for inspection is slow, while letting it go direct is unpoliced. FortiSASE moves inspection into a cloud-delivered service so the same web filtering, application access and data policy applies wherever the user sits. What makes it work is not the technology but the inventory: policy can only be authored once someone has written down which applications exist and who may reach each of them.

benefits.text: One access policy applies to depot, roaming and home users rather than three different ones
benefits.limits: Consistency is a property of the policy, not of the platform; a policy authored per-population in the new console reproduces the old problem in a new place

benefits.text: Private application access is granted per application instead of by placing a user on the network
benefits.limits: Only for applications that can be published through the access proxy; legacy protocols may still need a network path, and those exceptions should be named rather than absorbed

benefits.text: Depot sites stop needing a full inspection stack of their own
benefits.limits: Real only where the site stack is actually retired; running both is the common outcome and costs more than either

residency: Inspection runs in the vendor’s cloud points of presence, so the deployment region and log-storage location are a design decision that must be made explicitly, not a default

notFor.situation: An organisation already migrated onto another cloud-delivered secure access service
notFor.why: Policy does not port between services, so a second one means authoring the estate twice

notFor.situation: A workforce entirely inside inspected offices
notFor.why: The service solves the problem of users who are not behind the perimeter; if there are none, it adds a hop

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a migrated pilot population with policy under change control
Support model: Vendor subscription support for the service; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed policy operations.
1) Assessment — application and population inventory, identity readiness, residency position
2) Design — policy model, point-of-presence and log-region selection, publication plan, fallback
3) Pilot — one population migrated with the legacy path retained and measured
4) Migrate and hand over — remaining populations migrated, legacy platform decommissioned
deliverables: A user in any population receives the same policy decision for the same application
A private application is reachable only through the access proxy, verified by attempting the network path
Access logs for all populations are queryable in one place
